content: Cystex, a combination of methenamine, sodium salicylate, and benzoic acid, is prescribed as follows: Dosage: For individuals aged 16 years and older, the recommended dose is 2 tablets taken orally every 6 hours. The medication should be administered with meals and at bedtime. It is important to use this medication only after a urinary tract infection (UTI) has been eradicated using appropriate antibiotics. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established for individuals under 16 years of age. Methenamine: This component is indicated for the prophylaxis and suppression of chronic, recurrent UTIs when long-term therapy is required. Methenamine is hydrolyzed in acidic urine to produce ammonia and formaldehyde, which act as bactericidal agents. It does not convert to formaldehyde in the serum. Sodium Salicylate: This ingredient serves as an analgesic, providing pain relief. Benzoic Acid: This component exhibits weak antifungal and antibacterial properties. Additionally, it helps acidify the urine, which can enhance the effectiveness of methenamine. Pharmacokinetics: Absorption: Methenamine is well absorbed, with 10-30% hydrolyzed by gastric acid unless the tablet is enteric-coated. Metabolism: Approximately 10-25% of methenamine is metabolized by the liver. Excretion: About 90% of the drug is excreted in the urine. Half-Life: The half-life of methenamine is approximately 3-6 hours. Peak Urine Time: Formaldehyde levels peak in the urine at 2 hours for hippurate salts and 3-8 hours for mandelate salts. Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy Category C: Methenamine is classified as Category C, meaning that caution is advised as risk to the fetus cannot be ruled out. Controlled studies in pregnant women are lacking. Lactation: Methenamine is excreted in human breast milk. Caution is advised when administering this medication to breastfeeding mothers, as the risk to the infant cannot be excluded. This medication should be used with care and only under the guidance of a healthcare professional, particularly in populations such as pregnant or lactating individuals.
